newsitem.title: UK: WORLD BONDS - FOMC blocks road to recovery.
newsitem.headline: WORLD BONDS - FOMC blocks road to recovery.

text.p: U.S. employment data has put the brakes on the recent slide in international bond markets but interest rate uncertainty will keep investors at bay and curtail a full scale recovery, analysts said on Monday.
Investors are likely to hold back from bond markets until after the next meeting of the policy-setting U.S. Federal Open Market Committee (FOMC) meeting on March 25.

"There's so much event risk in the U.S./Germany spread, it's difficult to take a strong view on it," said Graham McDevitt, senior analyst at Paribas Capital Markets in London. The 10-year T-note/Bund yield spread edged back below 100 basis points from around 114 early last week after the release of February unemployment data.

February U.S. non-farm payrolls rose by 339,000 against a revised 247,000 in January. The unemployment rate fell to 5.3 from 5.4 percent and increased the likelihood of a rise in U.S. interest rates at the next FOMC meeting, analysts said.
But an $0.03 increase in average hourly earnings to $12.09 buoyed the bond market.
The U.S./German spread stood at 94 basis points at 1200 GMT on Monday, in a rising market for most European bonds.

The yield on the U.S. long bond rose from a low of around 6.63 percent on February 14 to a high of almost seven percent on March 6, before dipping on Friday. It was quoted at 6.82 percent at 1200 GMT.
The markets are oversold, analysts said, but investors will remain on the sidelines until later in the month.
"The FOMC is likely to overhang the markets -- there is not much upside from here," said Adrian Owens, European economist at Julius Baer Investments in London.
June Eurodollar futures are pricing in a rate rise by the end of the second quarter. The U.S. Federal funds rate stands at 5.25 percent.
"The market's money is going for May," said McDevitt. Following the March meeting, the next FOMC meeting will take place in May.
"Some of the data out last week have increased the likelihood of a March rise. If the Fed does not raise on March 25, the market could have a decent corrective rally," he added.
The dollar will have a major impact on European bond spreads ahead of the FOMC meeting, but European bonds have their own worries, analysts said.
"The peripheral European bond markets will still be focusing on EMU," said Keith Edmonds, chief analyst at IBJ International in London.
"European bonds will be looking closely at the comments after the Franco-German summit," he added.
The Franco-German Economic and Financial Council summit meeting takes place in Lyon on Wednesday.
European bonds will be nervous, analysts said, after weekend comments from German government adviser Herbert Hax that Germany should delay entry into European Economic and Monetary Union.
Italian Foreign Minister Lamberto Dini also said on Saturday he saw no risk of a delay to the planned 1999 start date of EMU, but did not rule out a delay to the decision on who should qualify.
But gilts have scope to outperform against Bunds this week, analysts said.

"The UK has got off to a good start after George's comments," said Owens. Bank of England governor Eddie George said in Basle on Monday he expected British inflation to reach the 2.5 percent target during 1997.
